blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__candidate_insights
      description: Candidate insights per opportunity combining stage depth, lifecycle timing, interview and feedback metrics with categorical labels
      grain: One row per opportunity_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_lever__opportunity as opportunity_metrics: - Select opportunity_id, contact_id, contact_name, stage_id, owner_user_id, created_at, last_advanced_at, last_interaction_at, archived_at. - total_lifecycle_days = (last_interaction_at - created_at) expressed in days; if either timestamp is missing, set to 0. - days_to_last_advancement = (last_advanced_at - created_at) in days; if either timestamp is missing, set to 0. - is_archived = 1 when archived_at is present, else 0. - Build interview_summary from staging.stg_lever__interview grouped by opportunity_id: - total_interviews = count of all interview rows (including canceled). - completed_interviews = count where canceled_at is absent. - canceled_interviews = count where canceled_at is present. - avg_interview_duration = average of duration over all rows (canceled included; missing durations ignored by the aggregate). - total_interview_time = sum of duration over all rows (canceled included; missing durations ignored by the aggregate). - Build feedback_summary by left joining interviews to interview_feedback on interview_id, grouped by opportunity_id: - total_feedback = distinct count of feedback_form_id (missing form IDs excluded). - completed_feedback = distinct count of feedback_form_id (same as total_feedback in this logic). - positive_feedback = 0; negative_feedback = 0 (placeholders). - Build stage_quality from staging.stg_lever__stage: - current_stage = stage_name. - current_stage_order by case-insensitive substring mapping; first match applies: ''new''/''lead''→1; ''screen''/''phone''→2; ''technical''/''coding''→3; ''onsite''/''final''→4; ''offer''→5; ''hire''/''accept''→6; otherwise 0. - Final assembly: - Left join opportunity_metrics to interview_summary (by opportunity_id), feedback_summary (by opportunity_id), and stage_quality (by stage_id). - Set missing interview and feedback aggregates to 0. - interview_completion_rate = completed_interviews / total_interviews as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if total_interviews = 0 then 0.0. - feedback_completion_rate = completed_feedback / total_feedback as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if total_feedback = 0 then 0.0. - positive_feedback_rate = positive_feedback / completed_feedback as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if completed_feedback = 0 then 0.0. - candidate_quality_score (0–100) = sum of: - Stage depth: 25 when current_stage_order ≥ 3; otherwise current_stage_order × 8. - Time efficiency: 25 when total_lifecycle_days ≤ 30; 15 when ≤ 60; otherwise 5. - Interview completion: 25 when total_interviews > 0 and completed_interviews / total_interviews ≥ 80%; otherwise 10. - Feedback quality: 25 when total_feedback > 0 and positive_feedback / completed_feedback ≥ 60% (treat zero completed as not meeting the threshold); otherwise 10. - Round the total to the nearest integer and clamp to the 0–100 range; if current_stage_order is missing, the stage-depth component is missing and the overall score becomes NULL. - process_speed_category by total_lifecycle_days: ≤14 → "Fast Track (≤14 days)"; 15–30 → "Standard (15-30 days)"; 31–60 → "Extended (31-60 days)"; >60 → "Long Process (>60 days)". - candidate_status_category precedence: - If is_archived = 1 and current_stage_order ≥ 5 → "Successfully Hired". - Else if is_archived = 1 and current_stage_order ≥ 3 → "Advanced but Not Hired". - Else if is_archived = 1 → "Early Stage Rejection". - Else if current_stage_order ≥ 4 → "In Final Stages". - Else if current_stage_order ≥ 2 → "In Progress". - Else → "Early Stage". - Note: a missing current_stage_order does not satisfy any threshold comparisons. - candidate_experience_quality precedence: - If canceled_interviews > 0 → "Poor Experience (Cancellations)". - Else if feedback_completion_rate ≥ 80.0 and interview_completion_rate ≥ 90.0 → "Excellent Experience". - Else if feedback_completion_rate ≥ 60.0 and interview_completion_rate ≥ 80.0 → "Good Experience". - Else → "Standard Experience". - calculated_at = the query execution timestamp. - Output rows are ordered by candidate_quality_score descending, then total_lifecycle_days ascending.'
      columns:
      - name: opportunity_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique opportunity identifier; grouping key with exactly one row per value
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: contact_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate contact identifier from opportunity record
      - name: contact_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate name from opportunity; casing and whitespace preserved
      - name: stage_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current stage_id from opportunity used to join stage metadata
      - name: current_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stage name from stage metadata; NULL if stage_id not found
      - name: current_stage_order
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Stage order from keyword mapping (0–6); NULL if stage_id not found
      - name: owner_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Opportunity owner user identifier from opportunity
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Opportunity creation timestamp from source
      - name: total_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days from created_at to last_interaction_at (fractional); 0 when either timestamp is missing
      - name: days_to_last_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days from created_at to last_advanced_at (fractional); 0 when either timestamp is missing
      - name: is_archived
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Archive flag from archived_at (1 when present, else 0)
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of all interviews for the opportunity (includes canceled; 0 if none)
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of interviews without a cancellation; 0 if none
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of interviews with a cancellation; 0 if none
      - name: interview_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completed_interviews divided by total_interviews as percent (0–100) rounded to 1 decimal; 0.0 when total_interviews=0
      - name: avg_interview_duration
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average interview duration over all interviews (canceled included; missing durations ignored); 0.0 if none
      - name: total_interview_time
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Sum of interview duration over all interviews (canceled included; missing durations ignored); 0.0 if none
      - name: total_feedback
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of feedback_form_id joined via interviews; missing form IDs excluded; 0 if none
      - name: completed_feedback
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of feedback_form_id (same as total_feedback in this logic); 0 if none
      - name: positive_feedback
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Placeholder count of positive feedback (always 0 in this logic)
      - name: negative_feedback
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Placeholder count of negative feedback (always 0 in this logic)
      - name: feedback_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completed_feedback divided by total_feedback as percent (0–100) rounded to 1 decimal; 0.0 when total_feedback=0
      - name: positive_feedback_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Positive_feedback divided by completed_feedback as percent (0–100) rounded to 1 decimal; 0.0 when completed_feedback=0
      - name: candidate_quality_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Composite score 0–100 from stage depth, time efficiency, interview completion, and feedback quality, rounded to integer and clamped; may be NULL if stage metadata is missing
      - name: process_speed_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Speed bucket by total_lifecycle_days: Fast Track (≤14), Standard (15–30), Extended (31–60), Long Process (>60)'
      - name: candidate_status_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Status by archive flag and stage order: Successfully Hired, Advanced but Not Hired, Early Stage Rejection, In Final Stages, In Progress, or Early Stage'
      - name: candidate_experience_quality
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Experience label by precedence: cancellations → Poor; else rates ≥80%/≥90% → Excellent; ≥60%/≥80% → Good; else Standard'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp when the model was computed (query execution time)

references.name: staging.stg_lever__opportunity
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_lever__opportunity as opportunity_metrics: - Select opportunity_id, contact_id, contact_name, stage_id, owner_user_id, created_at, last_advanced_at, last_interaction_at, archived_at. - total_lifecycle_days = (last_interaction_at - created_at) expressed in days; if either timestamp is missing, set to 0. - days_to_last_advancement = (last_advanced_at - created_at) in days; if either timestamp is missing, set to 0. - is_archived = 1 when archived_at is present, else 0. - Build interview_summary from staging.stg_lever__interview grouped by opportunity_id: - total_interviews = count of all interview rows (including canceled). - completed_interviews = count where canceled_at is absent. - canceled_interviews = count where canceled_at is present. - avg_interview_duration = average of duration over all rows (canceled included; missing durations ignored by the aggregate). - total_interview_time = sum of duration over all rows (canceled included; missing durations ignored by the aggregate). - Build feedback_summary by left joining interviews to interview_feedback on interview_id, grouped by opportunity_id: - total_feedback = distinct count of feedback_form_id (missing form IDs excluded). - completed_feedback = distinct count of feedback_form_id (same as total_feedback in this logic). - positive_feedback = 0; negative_feedback = 0 (placeholders). - Build stage_quality from staging.stg_lever__stage: - current_stage = stage_name. - current_stage_order by case-insensitive substring mapping; first match applies: ''new''/''lead''→1; ''screen''/''phone''→2; ''technical''/''coding''→3; ''onsite''/''final''→4; ''offer''→5; ''hire''/''accept''→6; otherwise 0. - Final assembly: - Left join opportunity_metrics to interview_summary (by opportunity_id), feedback_summary (by opportunity_id), and stage_quality (by stage_id). - Set missing interview and feedback aggregates to 0. - interview_completion_rate = completed_interviews / total_interviews as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if total_interviews = 0 then 0.0. - feedback_completion_rate = completed_feedback / total_feedback as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if total_feedback = 0 then 0.0. - positive_feedback_rate = positive_feedback / completed_feedback as a percent rounded to 1 decimal; if completed_feedback = 0 then 0.0. - candidate_quality_score (0–100) = sum of: - Stage depth: 25 when current_stage_order ≥ 3; otherwise current_stage_order × 8. - Time efficiency: 25 when total_lifecycle_days ≤ 30; 15 when ≤ 60; otherwise 5. - Interview completion: 25 when total_interviews > 0 and completed_interviews / total_interviews ≥ 80%; otherwise 10. - Feedback quality: 25 when total_feedback > 0 and positive_feedback / completed_feedback ≥ 60% (treat zero completed as not meeting the threshold); otherwise 10. - Round the total to the nearest integer and clamp to the 0–100 range; if current_stage_order is missing, the stage-depth component is missing and the overall score becomes NULL. - process_speed_category by total_lifecycle_days: ≤14 → "Fast Track (≤14 days)"; 15–30 → "Standard (15-30 days)"; 31–60 → "Extended (31-60 days)"; >60 → "Long Process (>60 days)". - candidate_status_category precedence: - If is_archived = 1 and current_stage_order ≥ 5 → "Successfully Hired". - Else if is_archived = 1 and current_stage_order ≥ 3 → "Advanced but Not Hired". - Else if is_archived = 1 → "Early Stage Rejection". - Else if current_stage_order ≥ 4 → "In Final Stages". - Else if current_stage_order ≥ 2 → "In Progress". - Else → "Early Stage". - Note: a missing current_stage_order does not satisfy any threshold comparisons. - candidate_experience_quality precedence: - If canceled_interviews > 0 → "Poor Experience (Cancellations)". - Else if feedback_completion_rate ≥ 80.0 and interview_completion_rate ≥ 90.0 → "Excellent Experience". - Else if feedback_completion_rate ≥ 60.0 and interview_completion_rate ≥ 80.0 → "Good Experience". - Else → "Standard Experience". - calculated_at = the query execution timestamp. - Output rows are ordered by candidate_quality_score descending, then total_lifecycle_days ascending.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__candidate_lifecycle
      description: Simplified candidate lifecycle metrics per opportunity with stage flags and time-based durations.
      grain: One row per opportunity × application (left join on opportunity_id); if no application exists, one row per opportunity.
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_lever__opportunity (opp). - Left join staging.stg_lever__application (a) on opportunity_id to bring posting_id. - Left join staging.stg_lever__stage (st) on stage_id to bring stage_name. - Pass-through fields: opportunity_id, contact_id, posting_id, current_stage_id (opp.stage_id), current_stage_name (st.stage_name), archived_at, archived_reason_id, last_interaction_at, last_advanced_at. - Durations are in days, computed as seconds difference divided by 86,400 with no rounding: - total_lifecycle_days: from created_at to archived_at if archived_at is present; otherwise from created_at to the current timestamp. - days_since_last_advancement: from created_at to last_advanced_at if present; otherwise from created_at to the current timestamp. - avg_days_per_stage: from created_at to the current timestamp. - Timestamps are parsed as timestamps; if created_at is missing/invalid, these results are null. Values depend on the current timestamp at execution. - Constants: - total_stages_passed = 1. - total_interviews = 0, completed_interviews = 0, canceled_interviews = 0, avg_interview_duration_minutes = 0, total_interview_time_minutes = 0. - total_feedback_count = 0, completed_feedback_count = 0, feedback_completion_rate_pct = null, avg_recommendation_score = null, all_recommendations = null. - total_interactions = 0, last_interaction_type = null, communication_frequency_score = 1. - Flags: - is_archived = 1 if archived_at is present, else 0. - is_hired = 1 if the stage name (case-insensitive) contains "hire" or "accept", else 0; null stage name is treated as 0. - has_offer = 1 if the stage name (case-insensitive) contains "offer", else 0; null stage name is treated as 0. - calculated_at is the current timestamp at query execution. - No aggregation or de-duplication is applied; multiple application rows per opportunity produce multiple output rows.'
      columns:
      - name: opportunity_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Opportunity identifier from opportunities; not unique due to potential multiple applications per opportunity.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: contact_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact identifier associated with the opportunity.
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting identifier from applications; null if no matching application.
      - name: current_stage_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current stage identifier from opportunities.
      - name: current_stage_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stage name from stages joined by stage_id; null if no match.
      - name: archived_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the opportunity was archived; null if not archived.
      - name: archived_reason_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Archive reason identifier from opportunities; may be null.
      - name: last_interaction_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the last interaction on the opportunity; may be null.
      - name: last_advanced_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the last stage advancement; may be null.
      - name: total_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Unrounded days from created_at to archived_at, else to now; null if created_at is missing/invalid.
      - name: days_since_last_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Unrounded days from created_at to last_advanced_at, else to now; null if created_at is missing/invalid.
      - name: total_stages_passed
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 1.
      - name: avg_days_per_stage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Unrounded days from created_at to now; null if created_at is missing/invalid.
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: avg_interview_duration_minutes
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: total_interview_time_minutes
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: total_feedback_count
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: completed_feedback_count
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant value 0.
      - name: feedback_completion_rate_pct
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Always null in this version.
      - name: avg_recommendation_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Always null in this version.
      - name: all_recommendations
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Always null in this version.
      - name: is_archived
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if archived_at is present, else 0.
      - name: is_hired
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if stage name contains 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive), else 0; null stage name treated as 0.

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__hiring_funnel_metrics
      description: 'Hiring funnel metrics per posting: conversion rates, time-to-stage averages, bottleneck label, efficiency grade, and calculation timestamp'
      grain: One row per posting_id with at least 3 applications
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity_stage_history
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      business_logic: '1) Stage normalization: - From staging.stg_lever__stage, map each lowercased stage_name to stage_order and stage_category: 1=Top of Funnel (''lead'' or ''new''), 2=Initial Screening (''phone'' or ''screening''), 3=Technical Assessment (''technical'' or ''coding''), 4=Final Interview (''onsite'' or ''final''), 5=Offer Stage (''offer''), 6=Hired (''hire'' or ''accept''), else 99 and ''Other''. 2) Opportunity-stage timeline: - Join staging.stg_lever__opportunity_stage_history to the mapping by stage_id. - Per opportunity_id ordered by updated_at, record stage_entered_at=updated_at and compute sequence markers (row number, previous, next). 3) Funnel progression per opportunity: - For each opportunity_id, take the earliest timestamp of entering each normalized stage (orders 1–6). - highest_stage_reached = the maximum stage_order visited; unique_stages_visited = distinct stage_id count. - Reached flags for each stage are 1 if highest_stage_reached is at least that stage''s order, else 0. 4) Posting-level funnel metrics: - Join applications (a) to postings (p) by posting_id; left join per-opportunity funnel results by opportunity_id. - Group by posting_id, posting_title, categories_department/team/location/level. - Use distinct opportunity_id in all counts: total_applications = distinct opportunities per posting. reached_*_count = distinct opportunities where the corresponding reached flag = 1. - Conversion rates are percentages (0–100), rounded to two decimal places; if the denominator is zero, return 0: application_to_screening_rate = reached_screening_count / total_applications * 100; screening_to_technical_rate = reached_technical_count / reached_screening_count * 100; technical_to_final_rate = reached_final_count / reached_technical_count * 100; final_to_offer_rate = reached_offer_count / reached_final_count * 100; offer_to_hired_rate = reached_hired_count / reached_offer_count * 100; application_to_hired_rate = reached_hired_count / total_applications * 100. 5) Time-to-conversion per opportunity: - Durations in days are computed as the difference between the later and earlier stage-entered timestamps converted from seconds to days (divide by 86,400); if either timestamp is missing, the duration is NULL: days_to_screening: top of funnel → screening; days_screening_to_technical: screening → technical; days_technical_to_final: technical → final; days_final_to_offer: final → offer; days_offer_to_hired: offer → hired; total_days_to_hire: top of funnel → hired. 6) Final enrichments per posting: - For each posting_id, average the per-opportunity durations where the metric is not NULL, rounded to one decimal place: avg_days_to_screening, avg_days_screening_to_technical, avg_total_days_to_hire. - primary_bottleneck is determined by ordered threshold checks; the first match is chosen: if application_to_screening_rate < 50 → Initial Screening Bottleneck; else if screening_to_technical_rate < 60 → Technical Assessment Bottleneck; else if technical_to_final_rate < 70 → Final Interview Bottleneck; else if final_to_offer_rate < 80 → Offer Decision Bottleneck; else if offer_to_hired_rate < 70 → Offer Acceptance Bottleneck; else → No Major Bottleneck. - hiring_efficiency_grade is based on application_to_hired_rate: High Efficiency (≥10%), Medium Efficiency (5–10%), Low Efficiency (2–5%), Very Low Efficiency (<2%). - calculated_at is set to the current timestamp. - Filter: include only postings with total_applications ≥ 3. - The final result is ordered by total_applications descending, then application_to_hired_rate descending.'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting identifier and grouping key; exactly one row per posting_id passing the sample-size filter
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: posting_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Job posting title from staging.stg_lever__posting
      - name: categories_department
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Department category of the posting
      - name: categories_team
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Team category of the posting
      - name: categories_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Seniority/level category of the posting
      - name: categories_location
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Location category of the posting
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities linked to the posting; minimum is 3 due to final filter
      - name: reached_screening_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities that reached screening (highest normalized stage ≥ 2)
      - name: reached_technical_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities that reached technical assessment (highest normalized stage ≥ 3)
      - name: reached_final_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities that reached final interview (highest normalized stage ≥ 4)
      - name: reached_offer_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities that reached offer stage (highest normalized stage ≥ 5)
      - name: reached_hired_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities that reached hired (highest normalized stage ≥ 6)
      - name: application_to_screening_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of applications that reached screening; rounded to two decimals; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: screening_to_technical_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of screened that reached technical; rounded to two decimals; 0 if reached_screening_count=0
      - name: technical_to_final_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of technical that reached final; rounded to two decimals; 0 if reached_technical_count=0
      - name: final_to_offer_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of final that reached offer; rounded to two decimals; 0 if reached_final_count=0
      - name: offer_to_hired_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of offers that reached hired; rounded to two decimals; 0 if reached_offer_count=0
      - name: application_to_hired_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of applications that reached hired; rounded to two decimals; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: avg_days_to_screening
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from top of funnel to screening for the posting; rounded to one decimal; NULL if no data
      - name: avg_days_screening_to_technical
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from screening to technical for the posting; rounded to one decimal; NULL if no data
      - name: avg_total_days_to_hire
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from top of funnel to hire for the posting; rounded to one decimal; NULL if no data
      - name: hiring_efficiency_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Based on application_to_hired_rate: High (≥10%), Medium (5–10%), Low (2–5%), Very Low (<2%)'
      - name: primary_bottleneck
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Determined by ordered checks: <50% screening, <60% technical, <70% final, <80% offer decision, <70% offer acceptance; first match else ''No Major Bottleneck'''
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp when metrics were computed (current timestamp at model run)

references.line_text: business_logic: '1) Stage normalization: - From staging.stg_lever__stage, map each lowercased stage_name to stage_order and stage_category: 1=Top of Funnel (''lead'' or ''new''), 2=Initial Screening (''phone'' or ''screening''), 3=Technical Assessment (''technical'' or ''coding''), 4=Final Interview (''onsite'' or ''final''), 5=Offer Stage (''offer''), 6=Hired (''hire'' or ''accept''), else 99 and ''Other''. 2) Opportunity-stage timeline: - Join staging.stg_lever__opportunity_stage_history to the mapping by stage_id. - Per opportunity_id ordered by updated_at, record stage_entered_at=updated_at and compute sequence markers (row number, previous, next). 3) Funnel progression per opportunity: - For each opportunity_id, take the earliest timestamp of entering each normalized stage (orders 1–6). - highest_stage_reached = the maximum stage_order visited; unique_stages_visited = distinct stage_id count. - Reached flags for each stage are 1 if highest_stage_reached is at least that stage''s order, else 0. 4) Posting-level funnel metrics: - Join applications (a) to postings (p) by posting_id; left join per-opportunity funnel results by opportunity_id. - Group by posting_id, posting_title, categories_department/team/location/level. - Use distinct opportunity_id in all counts: total_applications = distinct opportunities per posting. reached_*_count = distinct opportunities where the corresponding reached flag = 1. - Conversion rates are percentages (0–100), rounded to two decimal places; if the denominator is zero, return 0: application_to_screening_rate = reached_screening_count / total_applications * 100; screening_to_technical_rate = reached_technical_count / reached_screening_count * 100; technical_to_final_rate = reached_final_count / reached_technical_count * 100; final_to_offer_rate = reached_offer_count / reached_final_count * 100; offer_to_hired_rate = reached_hired_count / reached_offer_count * 100; application_to_hired_rate = reached_hired_count / total_applications * 100. 5) Time-to-conversion per opportunity: - Durations in days are computed as the difference between the later and earlier stage-entered timestamps converted from seconds to days (divide by 86,400); if either timestamp is missing, the duration is NULL: days_to_screening: top of funnel → screening; days_screening_to_technical: screening → technical; days_technical_to_final: technical → final; days_final_to_offer: final → offer; days_offer_to_hired: offer → hired; total_days_to_hire: top of funnel → hired. 6) Final enrichments per posting: - For each posting_id, average the per-opportunity durations where the metric is not NULL, rounded to one decimal place: avg_days_to_screening, avg_days_screening_to_technical, avg_total_days_to_hire. - primary_bottleneck is determined by ordered threshold checks; the first match is chosen: if application_to_screening_rate < 50 → Initial Screening Bottleneck; else if screening_to_technical_rate < 60 → Technical Assessment Bottleneck; else if technical_to_final_rate < 70 → Final Interview Bottleneck; else if final_to_offer_rate < 80 → Offer Decision Bottleneck; else if offer_to_hired_rate < 70 → Offer Acceptance Bottleneck; else → No Major Bottleneck. - hiring_efficiency_grade is based on application_to_hired_rate: High Efficiency (≥10%), Medium Efficiency (5–10%), Low Efficiency (2–5%), Very Low Efficiency (<2%). - calculated_at is set to the current timestamp. - Filter: include only postings with total_applications ≥ 3. - The final result is ordered by total_applications descending, then application_to_hired_rate descending.'

- name: int_lever__interview_feedback
      description: Interview records left-joined to feedback to add feedback_form_id and a copy of the matched interview_id.
      grain: One row per interview, repeated for each matching feedback; may further repeat if multiple feedback_form rows share the same feedback_form_id.
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback
      - staging.stg_lever__feedback_form
      business_logic: '- Use staging.stg_lever__interview as the base and pass through these columns without transformation: interview_id, opportunity_id, candidate_id, stage_id, panel_id, creator_user_id, subject, location, timezone, gcal_event_url, feedback_reminder, note, interview_date, created_at, canceled_at, duration. - Left join staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback on matching interview_id. - Add feedback_form_id from the feedback record. - Add feedback_interview_id as the interview_id from the matched feedback record. - If no feedback matches, feedback_form_id and feedback_interview_id are NULL. - If multiple feedback rows match an interview, emit one output row per match; duplicates are preserved and no ordering or de-duplication is applied. - Left join staging.stg_lever__feedback_form on matching feedback_form_id. - No columns are selected from the form table. - If feedback_form contains multiple rows for a feedback_form_id, rows are multiplied accordingly; no de-duplication. - No filters, transformations, or aggregations are applied; row order is unspecified.'

      - name: interview_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview identifier from the base table; used to match feedback.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: feedback_interview_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview identifier from the matched feedback; NULL when no feedback matched.
      - name: opportunity_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Opportunity identifier associated with the interview.
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Candidate identifier for the interview.
      - name: stage_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pipeline stage identifier at the time of the interview.
      - name: panel_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Panel identifier for the interview.
      - name: creator_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: User identifier for the interview creator.
      - name: interview_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Scheduled interview start timestamp.
      - name: duration
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Interview duration in source units.
      - name: subject
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview subject or title.
      - name: location
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview location.
      - name: timezone
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Time zone for the scheduled interview.
      - name: gcal_event_url
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Google Calendar event URL.
      - name: feedback_reminder
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Feedback reminder content sent to interviewers.
      - name: note
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview notes.
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Interview creation timestamp.
      - name: canceled_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Interview cancellation timestamp; NULL if not canceled.
      - name: feedback_form_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Feedback form identifier from the matched feedback; NULL when no feedback matched.

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__interviewer_performance
      description: Interviewer performance metrics over the last 365 days with activity, feedback, outcomes, and tier per interviewer
      grain: One row per interviewer_user_id for interviews within the last 365 days
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__user
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interview_feedback
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: 'Filters and joins - Only include interviews dated within the last 365 days. - Join users to interviewer_user by user_id, then to interviews by interview_id. - Left join interview_feedback by interview_id; left join opportunity by opportunity_id; left join stage by stage_id. - Group by user_id, user_name, email, access_role, and created_at (one row per interviewer). Activity and interview metrics - total_interviews: distinct count of interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is null. - canceled_interviews: distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is not null. - interviews_per_month: divide total_interviews by 12 and round to 1 decimal. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average interview duration rounded to 1 decimal; NULL durations are ignored; averages are computed over all joined rows, so interviews repeated by left joins are included. - last_interview_date: latest interview_date; first_interview_date: earliest interview_date within the 365-day window. - activity_status: Active if last_interview_date is within 30 days, Recently Active if within 90 days, else Inactive. Feedback metrics - total_feedback_given: distinct count of feedback forms linked to the interviewer’s interviews. - feedback_completion_rate (%): if total_interviews > 0, compute total_feedback_given divided by total_interviews times 100 and round to 1 decimal; otherwise return 0. - avg_feedback_completion_hours, avg_recommendation_score, avg_feedback_text_length: constant 0. Outcome metrics - total_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities linked to the interviewer’s interviews. - positive_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities where stage_name (case-insensitive) contains ''hire'', ''accept'', or ''offer''. - negative_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities where archived_at is not null. - positive_outcome_rate (%): percentage of positive_outcomes over total_outcomes rounded to 1 decimal; if total_outcomes is 0, return NULL. - advancement_rate (%): percentage of distinct opportunities where last_advanced_at is after the interview_date rounded to 1 decimal; if total_outcomes is 0, return NULL; NULL timestamps do not satisfy the comparison. Score and tier - overall_performance_score: only computed when total_interviews >= 10 and feedback_completion_rate >= 80; weight feedback completion rate 30%, positive outcome rate 40%, and advancement rate 30%, then round to 1 decimal; if any component is NULL the score is NULL. - performance_tier: Insufficient Data if total_interviews < 5; otherwise Excellent if feedback_completion_rate >= 90 and positive_outcome_rate >= 30; Good if >= 80 and >= 20; Average if >= 70 and >= 10; else Needs Improvement. Timestamps - calculated_at: set to the current timestamp at query runtime.'
      columns:
      - name: interviewer_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer user identifier from stg_lever__user.user_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: interviewer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer display name from stg_lever__user.user_name
      - name: interviewer_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer email from stg_lever__user.email
      - name: interviewer_role
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer access role from stg_lever__user.access_role
      - name: interviewer_joined_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: User account creation timestamp from stg_lever__user.created_at
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of interviews in the last 365 days
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is null
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is not null
      - name: interviews_per_month
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total interviews divided by 12 and rounded to 1 decimal
      - name: avg_interview_duration_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average interview duration rounded to 1 decimal; NULLs ignored; duplicates from left joins are included
      - name: last_interview_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Most recent interview_date within the 365-day window
      - name: first_interview_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest interview_date within the 365-day window
      - name: activity_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Active if last_interview_date within 30 days, Recently Active if within 90 days, else Inactive
      - name: total_feedback_given
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of feedback forms linked to the interviewer’s interviews
      - name: feedback_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of total_feedback_given over total_interviews rounded to 1 decimal; returns 0 when total_interviews is 0
      - name: avg_feedback_completion_hours
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant 0
      - name: avg_recommendation_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant 0
      - name: avg_feedback_text_length
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Constant 0
      - name: positive_outcomes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities with stage_name containing 'hire', 'accept', or 'offer' (case-insensitive)
      - name: negative_outcomes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities where archived_at is not null
      - name: total_outcomes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of opportunities linked to the interviewer’s interviews
      - name: positive_outcome_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of positive_outcomes over total_outcomes rounded to 1 decimal; returns NULL when total_outcomes is 0
      - name: advancement_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentage of distinct opportunities with last_advanced_at after the interview_date rounded to 1 decimal; returns NULL when total_outcomes is 0
      - name: overall_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted score computed only when total_interviews>=10 and feedback_completion_rate>=80; weights are 30% FCR, 40% POS, 30% ADV, rounded to 1 decimal; returns NULL if any component is NULL
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier thresholds: Insufficient Data, Excellent, Good, Average, or Needs Improvement'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Query execution timestamp

business_logic: 'Filters and joins - Only include interviews dated within the last 365 days. - Join users to interviewer_user by user_id, then to interviews by interview_id. - Left join interview_feedback by interview_id; left join opportunity by opportunity_id; left join stage by stage_id. - Group by user_id, user_name, email, access_role, and created_at (one row per interviewer). Activity and interview metrics - total_interviews: distinct count of interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is null. - canceled_interviews: distinct count of interviews where canceled_at is not null. - interviews_per_month: divide total_interviews by 12 and round to 1 decimal. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average interview duration rounded to 1 decimal; NULL durations are ignored; averages are computed over all joined rows, so interviews repeated by left joins are included. - last_interview_date: latest interview_date; first_interview_date: earliest interview_date within the 365-day window. - activity_status: Active if last_interview_date is within 30 days, Recently Active if within 90 days, else Inactive. Feedback metrics - total_feedback_given: distinct count of feedback forms linked to the interviewer’s interviews. - feedback_completion_rate (%): if total_interviews > 0, compute total_feedback_given divided by total_interviews times 100 and round to 1 decimal; otherwise return 0. - avg_feedback_completion_hours, avg_recommendation_score, avg_feedback_text_length: constant 0. Outcome metrics - total_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities linked to the interviewer’s interviews. - positive_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities where stage_name (case-insensitive) contains ''hire'', ''accept'', or ''offer''. - negative_outcomes: distinct count of opportunities where archived_at is not null. - positive_outcome_rate (%): percentage of positive_outcomes over total_outcomes rounded to 1 decimal; if total_outcomes is 0, return NULL. - advancement_rate (%): percentage of distinct opportunities where last_advanced_at is after the interview_date rounded to 1 decimal; if total_outcomes is 0, return NULL; NULL timestamps do not satisfy the comparison. Score and tier - overall_performance_score: only computed when total_interviews >= 10 and feedback_completion_rate >= 80; weight feedback completion rate 30%, positive outcome rate 40%, and advancement rate 30%, then round to 1 decimal; if any component is NULL the score is NULL. - performance_tier: Insufficient Data if total_interviews < 5; otherwise Excellent if feedback_completion_rate >= 90 and positive_outcome_rate >= 30; Good if >= 80 and >= 20; Average if >= 70 and >= 10; else Needs Improvement. Timestamps - calculated_at: set to the current timestamp at query runtime.'

- name: int_lever__opportunity_application
      description: Denormalized join of opportunities with applications (opportunity.* plus selected application fields)
      grain: One row per opportunity_id × application_id; if no application match, one row per opportunity_id with NULL application fields
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      business_logic: '- Load all columns from staging.stg_lever__opportunity (alias opportunity). - Load all columns from staging.stg_lever__application (alias application). - Left join application to opportunity on opportunity.opportunity_id = application.opportunity_id. - Select opportunity.* and the following application fields: application_id, comments, company, posting_hiring_manager_user_id, posting_id, posting_owner_user_id, referrer_user_id, requisition_id, and type as application_type. - No filtering, transformation, aggregation, or de-duplication is performed. - If multiple application rows match an opportunity_id, output one row per match; if none match, output a single row for the opportunity with NULL application columns. - All values are passed through unchanged from source. - No explicit ordering is applied; output row order is undefined.'

references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_lever__opportunity_application; include all columns and rows unchanged. - From staging.stg_lever__user (using user_id, user_name), perform three LEFT JOINs: - owner_user_id → user_id to populate opportunity_owner_name = user_name - referrer_user_id → user_id to populate referrer_name = user_name - posting_hiring_manager_user_id → user_id to populate hiring_manager_name = user_name - Join behavior: - LEFT JOIN preserves all application rows; unmatched users produce NULL name fields. - If multiple stg_lever__user rows share the same user_id, the application row multiplies accordingly; no de-duplication, selection, or ordering is applied. - No filtering, aggregation, or ordering is performed; all non-derived columns are direct passthrough values from opportunity_application. - Data/format policies: strings preserved as-is; booleans and timestamps are passed through unchanged; NULLs are preserved.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__posting_analytics
      description: Job posting performance and engagement analytics (one row per posting with application, interview, conversion, timing, and scoring metrics)
      grain: One row per posting_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      - staging.stg_lever__interviewer_user
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      business_logic: 'Build one row per posting_id by enriching posting attributes with application, interview, hiring, time-efficiency, and scoring metrics. 1) Posting base - From staging.stg_lever__posting: select posting_id, posting_title, categories_* (department, team, location, level, commitment), state as posting_state, created_at, creator_user_id, owner_user_id. 2) Application metrics (grouped by posting_id from staging.stg_lever__application) - total_applications: distinct applications. - unique_candidates: distinct candidates. - unique_opportunities: distinct opportunities. - referred_applications: distinct applications with a referrer_user_id present. - internal_applications: distinct applications where type is ''user''. - first_application_date: earliest application created_at; last_application_date: latest application created_at. - Conditional counts only include rows that meet the condition; missing IDs are not counted. 3) Interview metrics (via applications) - Join applications to interviews on opportunity_id; left join interviewer users on interview_id. - total_interviews_scheduled: distinct interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct interviews not canceled. - canceled_interviews: distinct interviews that were canceled. - unique_interviewers: distinct interviewer users. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average of interview duration. - total_interview_time_minutes: sum of interview duration. 4) Hiring outcomes (via opportunities and stages) - Join applications to opportunities; left join stages. - candidates_hired: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "hire" or "accept" (case-insensitive). - offers_extended: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "offer" (case-insensitive). - candidates_rejected: distinct opportunities that are archived. 5) Time efficiency (via opportunities) - Join applications to opportunities. - Keep only rows where last_advanced_at and application created_at exist. - For each kept row, compute day differences: • to advancement: days between last_advanced_at and application created_at • to last contact: days between last_interaction_at and application created_at (missing last_interaction_at are ignored in averages) - Aggregate per posting_id: • avg_days_to_advancement: mean days to advancement • avg_days_to_last_contact: mean days to last contact over the same filtered set • median_days_to_advancement: 50th percentile of days to advancement 6) Final derivations (left-join metrics to posting base by posting_id; fill missing metrics with 0 where noted) - referral_rate_pct: referred_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - internal_application_rate_pct: internal_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - interview_completion_rate_pct: completed_interviews / total_interviews_scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled = 0. - application_to_hire_rate_pct: candidates_hired / total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications = 0. - offer_acceptance_rate_pct: candidates_hired / offers_extended × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended = 0. - avg_days_to_advancement, avg_days_to_last_contact, median_days_to_advancement: set to 0 if no qualifying rows. - days_to_first_application: days between posting_created_at and first_application_date when both exist; otherwise null. - posting_effectiveness_score (0–100): • min(20, total_applications) • +25 if candidates_hired > 0 • +20 if avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 30; +10 if ≤ 60; else +0 • +15 if interview_completion_rate_pct ≥ 80; else +5 • +10 if referral_rate_pct ≥ 20; +5 if ≥ 10; else +0 • +10 if offer_acceptance_rate_pct ≥ 70; else +0 Round to 0 decimals and clamp between 0 and 100. - performance_tier (first match): • High Performing: total_applications ≥ 20 AND candidates_hired ≥ 2 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 45 (treat missing as 999) • Good Performing: total_applications ≥ 10 AND candidates_hired ≥ 1 AND avg_days_to_advancement ≤ 60 (treat missing as 999) • Moderate Performing: total_applications ≥ 5 • Low Performing: total_applications ≥ 1 • Else: No Applications - primary_bottleneck (first match): • total_applications = 0 → No Attraction - Poor Job Posting • interview_completion_rate_pct < 70 → Interview Scheduling Issues • offer_acceptance_rate_pct < 60 AND offers_extended > 0 → Low Offer Acceptance • avg_days_to_advancement > 60 → Slow Decision Process • candidates_hired = 0 AND total_applications ≥ 10 → High Standards or Poor Fit • Else → No Major Issues - calculated_at: current timestamp at run time (time zone aware). - Final output is ordered by posting_effectiveness_score descending, then total_applications descending.'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique job posting identifier; exactly one output row per posting_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: posting_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Job posting title
      - name: categories_department
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: department'
      - name: categories_team
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: team'
      - name: categories_location
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: location'
      - name: categories_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: level'
      - name: categories_commitment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Posting category: commitment'
      - name: posting_state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting state
      - name: posting_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Posting creation timestamp
      - name: creator_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Creator user identifier
      - name: owner_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner user identifier
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct applications per posting; 0 if none
      - name: unique_candidates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct candidates per posting; 0 if none
      - name: unique_opportunities
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities per posting; 0 if none
      - name: referred_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct applications with a referrer present; 0 if none
      - name: internal_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct applications submitted by internal users (type='user'); 0 if none
      - name: referral_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Referred_applications divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: internal_application_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Internal_applications divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: total_interviews_scheduled
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews linked via applications; 0 if none
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews not canceled; 0 if none
      - name: canceled_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviews that were canceled; 0 if none
      - name: unique_interviewers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct interviewer users across associated interviews; 0 if none
      - name: interview_completion_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Completed_interviews divided by total_interviews_scheduled times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled=0
      - name: avg_interview_duration_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average interview duration in minutes; 0 if no interviews
      - name: total_interview_time_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total interview duration in minutes; 0 if no interviews
      - name: candidates_hired
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities in a stage whose name contains 'hire' or 'accept' (case-insensitive); 0 if none
      - name: offers_extended
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities in a stage whose name contains 'offer' (case-insensitive); 0 if none
      - name: candidates_rejected
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct opportunities that were archived; 0 if none
      - name: application_to_hire_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Candidates_hired divided by total_applications times 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications=0
      - name: offer_acceptance_rate_pct
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Candidates_hired divided by offers_extended times 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended=0
      - name: avg_days_to_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from application to last advancement over rows where both timestamps exist; 0 if none
      - name: avg_days_to_last_contact
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from application to last interaction within rows where last_advanced_at and created_at exist; 0 if none
      - name: median_days_to_advancement
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Median (50th percentile) days from application to last advancement; 0 if none
      - name: days_to_first_application
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Days from posting_created_at to the first application; NULL if either timestamp is missing
      - name: posting_effectiveness_score
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Composite 0–100 score from application volume, hires, speed, interview completion, referrals, and offer acceptance; rounded to 0 decimals and clamped
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tier assigned from thresholds on applications, hires, and average days to advancement
      - name: primary_bottleneck
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Primary bottleneck based on ordered checks: attraction, interview completion, offer acceptance, decision speed, or fit/standards'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp when the row is computed (time zone aware)

references.name: staging.stg_lever__posting
references.line_text: business_logic: 'Build one row per posting_id by enriching posting attributes with application, interview, hiring, time-efficiency, and scoring metrics. 1) Posting base - From staging.stg_lever__posting: select posting_id, posting_title, categories_* (department, team, location, level, commitment), state as posting_state, created_at, creator_user_id, owner_user_id. 2) Application metrics (grouped by posting_id from staging.stg_lever__application) - total_applications: distinct applications. - unique_candidates: distinct candidates. - unique_opportunities: distinct opportunities. - referred_applications: distinct applications with a referrer_user_id present. - internal_applications: distinct applications where type is ''user''. - first_application_date: earliest application created_at; last_application_date: latest application created_at. - Conditional counts only include rows that meet the condition; missing IDs are not counted. 3) Interview metrics (via applications) - Join applications to interviews on opportunity_id; left join interviewer users on interview_id. - total_interviews_scheduled: distinct interviews. - completed_interviews: distinct interviews not canceled. - canceled_interviews: distinct interviews that were canceled. - unique_interviewers: distinct interviewer users. - avg_interview_duration_minutes: average of interview duration. - total_interview_time_minutes: sum of interview duration. 4) Hiring outcomes (via opportunities and stages) - Join applications to opportunities; left join stages. - candidates_hired: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "hire" or "accept" (case-insensitive). - offers_extended: distinct opportunities whose stage name contains "offer" (case-insensitive). - candidates_rejected: distinct opportunities that are archived. 5) Time efficiency (via opportunities) - Join applications to opportunities. - Keep only rows where last_advanced_at and application created_at exist. - For each kept row, compute day differences: • to advancement: days between last_advanced_at and application created_at • to last contact: days between last_interaction_at and application created_at (missing last_interaction_at are ignored in averages) - Aggregate per posting_id: • avg_days_to_advancement: mean days to advancement • avg_days_to_last_contact: mean days to last contact over the same filtered set • median_days_to_advancement: 50th percentile of days to advancement 6) Final derivations (left-join metrics to posting base by posting_id; fill missing metrics with 0 where noted) - referral_rate_pct: referred_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - internal_application_rate_pct: internal_applications / total_applications × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_applications = 0. - interview_completion_rate_pct: completed_interviews / total_interviews_scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if total_interviews_scheduled = 0. - application_to_hire_rate_pct: candidates_hired / total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; 0 if total_applications = 0. - offer_acceptance_rate_pct: candidates_hired / offers_extended × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 0 if offers_extended = 0. - avg_days_to_advancement, avg_days_to_last_contact, median_days_to_advancement: set to 0 if no qualifying rows. - days_to_first_application: days between posting_created_at and first_application_date when both exist; - name: int_lever__posting_applications
      description: Aggregates application metrics per posting and selects the latest hiring manager user ID by created_at.
      grain: One row per non-null posting_id with applications in staging.stg_lever__application
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      business_logic: '- Read all application rows from staging.stg_lever__application. - Aggregate per posting_id: - first_app_sent_at: the earliest non-null created_at; if all created_at values are NULL, this is NULL. - count_referred_applications: number of rows where type equals ''referral''; exact match, NULL or other values do not count. - count_posting_applications: number of rows where type equals ''posting'' or ''agency''; exact matches only. - count_manual_user_applications: number of rows where type equals ''user''; exact match. - count_opportunities: number of distinct non-null opportunity_id. - count_open_opportunities: number of distinct non-null opportunity_id where archived_at is NULL. - Determine posting_hiring_manager_user_id by selecting, for each posting_id, the application with the latest created_at; if multiple rows share the same created_at or created_at is NULL, tie-breaking and NULL ordering follow the engine defaults; take that row''s posting_hiring_manager_user_id (may be NULL). - Inner join the aggregates with the latest-application selection on posting_id; posting_id values that are NULL do not match and are excluded, and only posting_ids with at least one application appear. - Output one row per non-null posting_id present in the application data.'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Grouping key; one row per non-null posting_id with applications
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: first_app_sent_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest application created_at timestamp for the posting_id; NULL if all created_at are NULL
      - name: count_referred_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type exactly 'referral' for the posting_id
      - name: count_posting_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type 'posting' or 'agency' for the posting_id
      - name: count_manual_user_applications
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of application rows with type exactly 'user' for the posting_id
      - name: count_opportunities
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of non-null opportunity_id for the posting_id
      - name: count_open_opportunities
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of non-null opportunity_id with archived_at NULL for the posting_id
      - name: posting_hiring_manager_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: User ID from the application with the latest created_at for the posting_id; ties are resolved arbitrarily

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_lever__posting_performance
      description: Job posting performance metrics by posting, including applications, candidates, interviews, conversion rates, score, and status
      grain: One row per posting_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_lever__posting
      - staging.stg_lever__application
      - staging.stg_lever__opportunity
      - staging.stg_lever__stage
      - staging.stg_lever__contact_email
      - staging.stg_lever__contact_phone
      - staging.stg_lever__resume
      - staging.stg_lever__interview
      business_logic: 'For each posting in staging.stg_lever__posting: - Left join applications on posting_id; left join opportunities on application.opportunity_id; left join contact_email/phone on opportunity.contact_id; left join resume on application.opportunity_id; left join interview on application.opportunity_id. - All counting metrics use unique counts to avoid double-counting from joins. - Application metrics: - total_applications = unique applications; unique_candidates = unique candidates; unique_opportunities = unique opportunities. - first_application_date = earliest application.created_at; last_application_date = latest application.created_at; both null when no applications. - referred_applications = unique applications with a referrer. - internal_applications = unique applications where type is user; external_applications = unique applications where type is candidate. - referral_rate = if total_applications > 0 then referred_applications ÷ total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Time metric: - days_to_first_application = fractional days between posting_created_at and first_application_date; computed only when both timestamps can be parsed; otherwise null. - Stage-based candidate metrics (stage membership determined by stage_name keywords, case-insensitive): - Interview-like: stage_name contains interview, technical, or onsite; Offer-like: contains offer; Hire-like: contains hire or accept. - candidates_reached_interview/offer/hired = unique opportunities currently in the corresponding stage group. - active_candidates_30d = unique opportunities with last_interaction_at within the last 30 days relative to the query date (unparsable timestamps are ignored). - archived_candidates = unique opportunities with archived_at present. - candidates_with_email/phone/resume = unique opportunities where the linked contact has an email/phone, or a resume exists, respectively. - Interview efficiency: - total_interviews_scheduled = unique interviews; completed_interviews = unique interviews not canceled; canceled_interviews = unique interviews canceled. - interview_completion_rate = if any interviews then completed ÷ scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - avg_interviews_per_candidate = if any opportunities then scheduled interviews ÷ unique_opportunities, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - Conversion rates: - application_to_interview/offer/hire_rate = if total_applications > 0 then (unique opportunities reaching interview/offer/hire ÷ total_applications) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - offer_to_hire_rate = if any offers then (unique opportunities reaching hire ÷ unique opportunities reaching offer) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Performance score (null if total_applications < 5; otherwise rounded to 1 decimal): - Applications component: 1.25 points per application capped at 25. - Hire presence: +25 if any hire-like opportunity exists; else +0. - Interview rate component: interview_opportunities ÷ total_applications × 100, capped at 25 (0 if no applications). - Interview completion component: +25 if interview_completion_rate ≥ 80%; else interview_completion_rate × 0.3125. - Sum the four components and round to 1 decimal. - Performance tier: - If total_applications = 0 → No Applications. - Else if total_applications < 5 → Low Volume. - Else if any hire-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 10 → High Performing. - Else if any offer-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 5 → Moderate Performing. - Else if any interview-like opportunity → Building Pipeline. - Else → Needs Attention. - Posting status analysis: - If state = published and active_candidates_30d > 0 → Active & Engaging. - Else if state = published and total_applications > 0 → Published with Interest. - Else if state = published → Published but No Interest. - Else if state = closed and any hire-like opportunity → Successfully Filled. - Else if state = closed → Closed without Hire. - Else → Unknown Status. - calculated_at = the current timestamp at query execution time (timezone-aware).'
      columns:
      - name: posting_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting identifier; grouping key with exactly one output row per posting_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: posting_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting title from stg_lever__posting.posting_title
      - name: categories_department
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Department category from stg_lever__posting.categories_department
      - name: categories_team
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Team category from stg_lever__posting.categories_team
      - name: categories_location
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Location category from stg_lever__posting.categories_location
      - name: categories_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Level category from stg_lever__posting.categories_level
      - name: categories_commitment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Commitment category from stg_lever__posting.categories_commitment
      - name: posting_state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Posting state from stg_lever__posting.state with no transformation
      - name: posting_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Posting creation timestamp from stg_lever__posting.created_at
      - name: creator_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Creator user identifier from stg_lever__posting.creator_user_id
      - name: owner_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner user identifier from stg_lever__posting.owner_user_id
      - name: requisition_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Requisition code from stg_lever__posting.requisition_code
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique applications linked to the posting; join duplicates do not inflate the count
      - name: unique_candidates

references.line_text: business_logic: 'For each posting in staging.stg_lever__posting: - Left join applications on posting_id; left join opportunities on application.opportunity_id; left join contact_email/phone on opportunity.contact_id; left join resume on application.opportunity_id; left join interview on application.opportunity_id. - All counting metrics use unique counts to avoid double-counting from joins. - Application metrics: - total_applications = unique applications; unique_candidates = unique candidates; unique_opportunities = unique opportunities. - first_application_date = earliest application.created_at; last_application_date = latest application.created_at; both null when no applications. - referred_applications = unique applications with a referrer. - internal_applications = unique applications where type is user; external_applications = unique applications where type is candidate. - referral_rate = if total_applications > 0 then referred_applications ÷ total_applications × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Time metric: - days_to_first_application = fractional days between posting_created_at and first_application_date; computed only when both timestamps can be parsed; otherwise null. - Stage-based candidate metrics (stage membership determined by stage_name keywords, case-insensitive): - Interview-like: stage_name contains interview, technical, or onsite; Offer-like: contains offer; Hire-like: contains hire or accept. - candidates_reached_interview/offer/hired = unique opportunities currently in the corresponding stage group. - active_candidates_30d = unique opportunities with last_interaction_at within the last 30 days relative to the query date (unparsable timestamps are ignored). - archived_candidates = unique opportunities with archived_at present. - candidates_with_email/phone/resume = unique opportunities where the linked contact has an email/phone, or a resume exists, respectively. - Interview efficiency: - total_interviews_scheduled = unique interviews; completed_interviews = unique interviews not canceled; canceled_interviews = unique interviews canceled. - interview_completion_rate = if any interviews then completed ÷ scheduled × 100, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - avg_interviews_per_candidate = if any opportunities then scheduled interviews ÷ unique_opportunities, rounded to 1 decimal; otherwise 0. - Conversion rates: - application_to_interview/offer/hire_rate = if total_applications > 0 then (unique opportunities reaching interview/offer/hire ÷ total_applications) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - offer_to_hire_rate = if any offers then (unique opportunities reaching hire ÷ unique opportunities reaching offer) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals; otherwise 0. - Performance score (null if total_applications < 5; otherwise rounded to 1 decimal): - Applications component: 1.25 points per application capped at 25. - Hire presence: +25 if any hire-like opportunity exists; else +0. - Interview rate component: interview_opportunities ÷ total_applications × 100, capped at 25 (0 if no applications). - Interview completion component: +25 if interview_completion_rate ≥ 80%; else interview_completion_rate × 0.3125. - Sum the four components and round to 1 decimal. - Performance tier: - If total_applications = 0 → No Applications. - Else if total_applications < 5 → Low Volume. - Else if any hire-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 10 → High Performing. - Else if any offer-like opportunity and total_applications ≥ 5 → Moderate Performing. - Else if any interview-like opportunity → Building Pipeline. - Else → Needs Attention. - Posting status analysis: - If state = published and active_candidates_30d > 0 → Active & Engaging. - Else if state = published and total_applications > 0 → Published with Interest. - Else if state = published → Published but No Interest. - Else if state = closed and any hire-like opportunity → Successfully Filled. - Else if state = closed → Closed without Hire. - Else → Unknown Status. - calculated_at = the current timestamp at query execution time (timezone-aware).'
